key.unknownVersionBehavior: reject with a visible unsupported-schema error

package.unknownVersionBehavior: reject with a visible unsupported-schema error

authenticatedEnvelope.unknownVersionBehavior: reject before key derivation or decryption

versioningRules: A format identifier is permanent and must not be reused for an incompatible document family.
A schema version changes whenever existing serialized fields change meaning, type, required status, or authenticated-data role.
Patch-level implementation releases may not silently reinterpret an existing serialized schema.
Unknown fields may be preserved by storage and transport layers but must not silently change algorithm behavior.
An authenticated-envelope field included in associated data may not be renamed, removed, or retyped without a new envelope schema version.
A migration must be explicit, one-directional, testable, and must retain the original document until the migrated output passes validation.
No migration may recover or infer missing secret material, masks, permutations, passphrases, salts, initialization vectors, or authentication tags.
A failed migration must leave the source document unchanged and produce a visible diagnostic.
migrationProcedure: Detect the exact format and schema version without modifying the source object.
Validate the source document with the validator written for that schema.
Copy the source into a new object; never mutate the only stored copy.
Apply one documented migration step at a time.
Assign the destination schema version only after all required destination fields exist.
Recompute fingerprints, checksums, or authenticated envelopes using the destination rules.
Validate the destination document with current validators.
Run positive, negative, corruption, and browser compatibility tests.
Record the migration in the phase ledger, source receipt, and validation contract before release.

authenticatedEnvelopeRules.migrationBoundary: An envelope cannot be migrated without opening it with the correct passphrase, validating the enclosed package, and sealing a new envelope with fresh random salt and IV.

releaseGate: Any new key, package, or envelope schema requires dedicated migration tests, updated browser verification, updated validation-contract minima, and passing main-branch CI evidence before the schema becomes current.
